strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Stages
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with local bidiagonal coupling and inverse coupling between each. Total of 8 all-reduce dispatches. Straightforward implementation with no fusion or overlapping—highest dispatch count but simplest structure and memory access pattern.

strategies.name: Fused Forward-Backward Coupling Pairs
strategies.desc: Fuses the forward bidiagonal coupling and backward inverse coupling into a single local operation before each all-reduce, reducing intermediate buffer allocations. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but fewer memory operations and better cache locality for the coupling/decoupling arithmetic, trading compute fusion for same communication cost.

strategies.name: Chunked Reduce-Scatter All-Gather Pattern
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pair (16 total collective dispatches), allowing each rank to compute only its shard's coupling locally during the scatter phase. Doubles dispatch count but enables parallelized local computation and potentially better network utilization through smaller per-dispatch payloads.

strategies.name: Pipelined Overlapping All-Reduce Waves
strategies.desc: Splits the tensor into independent chunks and pipelines multiple all-reduce stages across chunks, launching the next chunk's all-reduce before the current chunk's local coupling completes. Uses async collectives and requires careful buffer management; aims to overlap communication with local coupling computation, trading increased memory footprint for reduced wall-clock time.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level All-Reduce
strategies.desc:
Exploits potential node-level locality by performing intra-node all-reduce followed by inter-node all-reduce at each stage (16 total dispatches if 2-level, or uses multi-level reduction tree). Larger per-dispatch payload at node level but leverages faster intra-node interconnect (NVLink/local fabric) versus inter-node network, optimizing for hierarchical hardware topology.
